statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). NQ trades at 29,413.25, down 0.12%, after slipping the 29,426.75 floor that had held since the 22:00 UTC reopen and setting a new session low at 29,409.00. Price sits about four points above that low inside an 86-point range, and ES is on its own 7,680.00 low, so Tail lifts from 14 to 17 on a marginal extension rather than on observed trend. Stress rises to 68: the 10-year is 5.018%, above Monday's rejected 5.01% print, WTI is 103.01 near its session high, and a two-day Federal Reserve meeting opens today.
recommendation: Tail at 17 remains in the low band, so the mapped state is EA_ON for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. The lift from 14 records genuine new evidence: the overnight floor gave way, both NQ and ES sit on their session lows, and yields and crude are pushing the same direction. What is absent is the structure that defines a pathological path. The whole overnight range is 86.25 points, or 0.29%, across more than six hours; the extension below the old floor measures 18 points; and retracement is still visibly working elsewhere, with the Nikkei 432 points off its 64,101.00 high and Monday's cash index having recovered 259.5 points from its low. Stress is high at 68 because the energy and long-end backdrop is unresolved, but Stress alone does not change the mapped state. The narrow danger window from 13:00 to 15:00 UTC covers the US cash open and the first full cash hour, where an unretraced opening continuation would be most likely to appear.
headline: NQ slips the overnight floor to a fresh 29,409.00 low and sits four points above it while the 10-year clears 5% at 5.018% and WTI holds 103.01 into the opening day of the Fed meeting - Tail lifts to 17 with Stress high at 68
body:
The specific development of this hour is a marginal break rather than a trend. The floor at 29,426.75 that had contained trade since the 22:00 UTC reopen gave way, and NQ printed a new session low at 29,409.00 before settling at 29,413.25, down 36.25 points or 0.12% on the day. That is an 18-point extension of a range that now measures 86.25 points, or 0.29%, across more than six hours of Globex trade. NQ sitting four points above its session low is the amplifier this assessment weighs most carefully, because an index holding near an extreme is one of the few reliable precursors of a no-retracement path. What is missing is everything else that normally accompanies it: there is no sequence of failed retracements, no repeated extension, and no meaningful directional efficiency in a range this narrow. The honest reading is a slow drift in thin Asian liquidity, and Tail moves from 14 to 17 to record it without overstating it.

Cross-asset evidence has tightened into alignment, which is why Stress rises while the dominant mode stays mixed. The 10-year Treasury yield is 5.018%, above the 5.01% intraday print that was rejected on Monday, and the 2-year is 4.68%; the German 10-year is above 3.51%, its highest since 2009, and the Japanese 10-year has returned to 3%. WTI is 103.01, up 1.60%, trading near its 103.16 session high, with Brent around 106.96. The Saudi East-West pipeline, which had carried four to five million barrels a day as the principal bypass for a Strait of Hormuz partially closed since March, remains shut after the drone strikes of 11 September. ES at 7,680.25 is down 0.16% and also on its session low. Yields higher, crude higher and equity futures lower is a coherent risk impulse, and it is the reason this assessment is not treating the NQ low as noise.

The counterweight is that retracement continues to function everywhere it can be observed. The Nikkei is 63,669.01, up 0.28%, having given back 432 points from its 64,101.00 high after earlier trading as low as 63,067.18 - a full round trip inside one session. Monday's US cash session closed the Nasdaq-100 at 29,127.16, down 0.82%, but only after recovering 259.5 points from a 28,867.67 low, and beneath the index the session was a rotation rather than a liquidation, with the PHLX chip index down 5.9% after the leaders of several AI laboratories called publicly for a slowdown in development while software and communications names closed higher. Conflicting breadth of that kind reduces directional conviction and belongs in Stress, not in Tail. The VIX at 17.10, up 7.95% on the session, is elevated but nowhere near a level that implies disorderly repricing.

The forward path is dominated by scheduled checkpoints rather than by observed structure. The Federal Reserve opens a two-day meeting today with roughly nine chances in ten priced for a 25 basis point increase on Wednesday, which would be the first since 2023; that decision at 18:00 UTC on 16 September falls outside this 24-hour window, but the positioning around it does not. Within the window, weekly ADP prints at 12:15 UTC, the Empire State manufacturing index at 12:30 UTC, and a 20-year bond auction settles at 17:00 UTC, which carries more weight than usual with the 10-year above 5%. The conditional path therefore holds the low band through the Asian session and the European handover, enters the watch band from the European cash open, and peaks at 23 across the declared 13:00 to 15:00 UTC danger window, with a secondary lift to 22 for the auction. The condition that would change the assessment is specific and still absent: shallow or absent pullbacks, repeated extension after failed retracements, and NQ holding an extreme instead of returning into its range.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly assessments are available. Tail entered the window at 20, held a 19 to 23 range through the Asian session and the European handover, peaked at 26 during the European mid-morning chip-led decline and repeated 25 in the following hour, eased through midday, printed 26 again at the US cash open, then decayed through the afternoon and evening to a 14 to 16 plateau across the last seven hours as the opening decline was partly recovered. Stress fell from a 79 peak to a 65 to 66 plateau, and Confidence held between 86 and 89 throughout. The window contains three hours in the orange band, all tied to the chip-led decline, and no hour reached the red band.
outlookSummary: The conditional path holds the low band at 17 through the remainder of the Asian session, edges to 18 at the Tokyo close and 19 for the European opening auction, and enters the watch band at 20 from the European cash open. It holds 21 across the two European mid-morning hours that produced Monday's chip-led leg, eases to 20 through the midday lull, returns to 21 for the 12:15 and 12:30 UTC releases, and peaks at 23 across the declared 13:00 to 15:00 UTC danger window covering the US cash open and the first full cash hour. It eases to 21 and 20 through the US midday, lifts to 22 for the 20-year bond auction at 17:00 UTC, holds 21 through the post-auction reaction and the power hour, and returns to the low band at 19 for the cash close. It falls to 16 inside the futures maintenance halt, recovers to 17 across the Globex reopen and the Tokyo open, and settles at 16 into the final pre-decision hours. Stress tracks a 65 to 74 path with its peak inside the danger window, and Confidence decays from 88 to 73 with forecast horizon.
